headline: Corn ends the week at $4.56; crude up 3.8% to $103
lead: Corn ended the week at **$4.56**, down 4½ cents, and soybeans edged up to $12.56½. Grains barely moved, but crude gained 3.8% to $103.27. That is the number that reaches your fuel and fertilizer bills next season, not the corn price.
teaser: Grains were quiet Friday while crude gained 3.8% to $103.27.

one_number.context: Soybeans at $12.56½ against Dec corn at $4.56 give a ratio near 2.8. That favors beans when acres are planned for next spring.

sections.title: Grains finish the week quiet
sections.body:
- Dec corn fell 4½ cents to **$4.56** and Nov soybeans gained 3½ cents to $12.56½.
- USDA admitted a data error in its September corn report, but the 181.2-bushel yield forecast stands.
- Grain merchandisers are carrying bigger inventories and higher freight costs, which strains their working capital.
sections.so_what: Heavy stocks keep a lid on corn, and nothing Friday changed that.

sections.title: Cattle hold near highs
sections.body:
- October live cattle gained 0.1% to **$229.875** and feeders rose 0.6% to $348.325.
- Cash strength is driving the climb, though kill numbers are rising.
- September placements and marketings were the lowest for the month in series history, per the October Cattle on Feed report.
sections.so_what: Tight supplies are holding cattle up even as kills pick up.

sections.title: Crude gains; gas drops
sections.body:
- WTI crude gained 3.8% to **$103.27** as the Iran war keeps tanker freight at record highs.
- Natural gas fell 5.6% to $2.64, near the bottom of its 52-week range.
- Diesel and fertilizer costs follow crude, so higher oil matters for next season's input bills.
sections.so_what: Oil and gas moved opposite ways, so input costs depend on which one you buy.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA confirms screwworm in a Texas elk
outside_the_pit.body: USDA confirmed New World screwworm in an elk in Pecos County, the first detection in US wildlife. It matters for cattle movement and trade.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress. Harvest pace could add to the pressure on basis, which sits near seasonal lows.
Corn holding $4.56 versus a break lower would show whether big stocks are winning.
Export sales. Soybean sales near the 25 million ton China pace would support $12.50.

source_summary: CME Group settlements, USDA, AgWeb, Feedstuffs, Beef Magazine, OilPrice.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.82 vs $4.62 projected (+4.3%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.74 vs $11.09 projected (+14.9%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 23, figured the way USDA RMA does. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 24. Oct 1-31 window, most states.

facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
